comparison: Both evaluate microscopy evidence of cancer cell-macrophage interactions (C3, C21-C25). OpenEval finds the evidence strongly supportive of physical contact and disruption of sinus lining. Peer reviewers are uncertain, questioning whether data demonstrate 'adhesive cell-cell contact' versus 'mere proximity' and raising concerns about generalizability of the 4T1 breast cancer experiments (C24).

OpenEval R1 includes C20 (Siglec1 expression on SCS macrophages) as part of broader microscopy evidence. Peer R2 specifically evaluates C20 and finds it supported through macrophage depletion experiments, though notes the results text should be more explicit and direct co-staining would be useful.

Both evaluate sialylation and binding evidence (C27-C28, C30-C32). OpenEval finds strong biochemical support through lectin staining, adhesion assays, and sialidase treatment. Peer reviewers express uncertainty due to figure labeling errors that create confusion about which cell line has more sialylation, undermining confidence in the data presentation.

Both evaluate proliferation effects (C36-C37, C40, C43-C45). OpenEval finds robust validation through gain-of-function and loss-of-function approaches with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers also support these findings, noting the HEK293T overexpression and J774A.1 knockdown experiments adequately address proliferation and apoptosis effects.

Both evaluate ERK/AKT signaling pathway activation (C47-C50). OpenEval finds the Phosflow data supportive with bidirectional experimental design, though notes the mechanism linking Siglec1 to signaling is unclear. Peer reviewers are uncertain, stating 'not much of a shift in pERK and pAKT' and questioning biological relevance, requesting strong positive controls to validate the findings.

Both evaluate RNA-seq transcriptional profiling (C52-C57). OpenEval finds the data supportive with reasonable differential expression criteria, though notes lack of multiple testing correction. Peer reviewers also support the RNA sequencing data and pathway analysis without raising concerns, accepting it as evidence for the proliferation phenotype.

Both evaluate PLK1 activation evidence (C59, C61-C65). OpenEval finds complementary in vivo and in vitro evidence supportive despite modest fold-change and unclear mechanistic link. Peer reviewers also support the PLK1 data, only noting the need for proper labeling to distinguish siRNA from overexpression experiments.

Both evaluate St3gal3 knockout validation experiments (C6, C69-C80, C82). OpenEval finds comprehensive loss-of-function validation with strong specificity (affects metastasis but not primary tumor). Peer reviewers confirm the experiments validate that St3gal3 manipulation has no intrinsic effects on B16F10 behavior and that abrogating Siglec1 signaling impairs proliferation and survival in the SCS.

Both evaluate negative control experiments (C38, C41-C42). OpenEval finds these controls appropriately exclude paracrine signaling and indirect effects, strengthening the direct contact conclusion. Peer reviewers also accept these control experiments without challenge.

Both evaluate the overall mechanistic model (C85-C86, C89). OpenEval finds the model well-supported by collective experimental data and consistent with prior literature. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about interpretation, questioning terminology like 'pioneering metastatic cells' for cultured cells and noting concerns about generalizability and whether data truly confirm adhesive contact in vivo.

OpenEval evaluates broader implications about LN tropism and therapeutic potential (C92-C93) as uncertain, noting these extend beyond direct experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these speculative claims.

OpenEval identifies background/contextual claims (C1-C2, C8-C18, C26, C29, C34-C35, C46, C60, C67-C68, C83, C88) as supported established knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates C84 (inference about clinical observations) as supported and reasonable based on established observations and experimental findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this claim.
